page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-16-standardlssd is a virtual machine instance within the z4d server family. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance provides 126.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 7.88 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include any graphics processing units, and the complimentary public IPv4 address count is zero.

While the instance is classified under storage-optimized configurations, the local storage size is specified as None, though it lists NVMe SSD as the local storage type. This indicates that primary storage requirements must be met through network-attached storage or external block storage volumes, representing a tradeoff for workloads requiring massive local physical disk space. No benchmark performance data is available for this specific instance type, meaning its raw computational and memory throughput cannot be compared quantitatively against other instances in the same class.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 1:8 makes this instance class qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local physical storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance. This hardware profile is suitable for memory-intensive applications, database caching layers, enterprise applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute cores.
